newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ACT OVERPOWER WAIKATO IN SUPER 12.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ACT OVERPOWER WAIKATO IN SUPER 12.

text.p: Australian Capital Territory (ACT) secured their first semifinal appearance in the Super 12 rugby series on Friday with a 48-34 home victory over Waikato.
Wallaby winger Joe Roff raced in two second half tries to seal the match and set up a potential playoff with Wellington at Athletic Park next Sunday for home ground advantage in the semifinals.
ACT have a perfect record at home, with Friday's win achieving the unique feat of victories against all the current teams in the Super 12 series.

Leading 29-13 at half-time, ACT scored first in the second term through flanker Owen Finegan, but the tide began to turn with tries to replacement winger Eric Rush and flanker Aaron Hopa taking Waikato to within seven points.
ACT withstood 10 minutes of pressure before Roff scored twice within two minutes to seal the match for their 11th win at home in the series.
Rush scored a late try in the dying minutes, but by then ACT had cemented a place in their first Super 12 semifinal.

ACT's win ended Waikato's hopes of making the Super 12 semifinals beginning on May 23. The New Zealanders were in eighth place before the match with only a slight hope of forcing their way into the play-offs.
ACT in contrast boosted their chances of hosting a semifinal and jumped from third into outright second in the standings.
The top four teams qualify for the semifinals, with the leading two sides to host their play-off matches.

ACT - Stephen Larkham; Mitch Hardy, James Holbeck, Pat Howard, Joe Roff; David Knox, George Gregan; Troy Coker, Brett Robinson (captain), Owen Finegan, David Giffin, John Langford, Ewen McKenzie, Marco Caputo, Patricio Noriega.

Waikato - Matt Cooper; Bruce Reihana, Pina Alatini, Caleb Ralph, Scott McLeod; Ian Foster, Rhys Duggan; Deon Muir, Brett Sinkinson, Glenn Taylor, Ian Jones (captain), Aaron Hopa, Richard Loe, Greg Smith, Michael Collins.
